g8s-cr-001.value: Container C with foam best minimized thermal-energy transfer. It ended at 63°C, compared with 54°C for felt and 44°C with no insulation. Starting from 80°C, C cooled only 17°C, less than B's 26°C and A's 36°C, so the foam design retained the most thermal energy over the same 30 minutes.

g8s-cr-002.value: The equal 36.0 g total mass before and after supports conservation of matter because the reaction occurred in a sealed system where no matter entered or left. Forming a gas and a new solid changes how the atoms are combined and arranged, but the same atoms remain in the closed system, so their total mass stays 36.0 g.

g8s-cr-003.value: Greater food availability was associated with larger beetle populations: 5, 10, 20, and 30 g/day produced 17, 30, 46, and 48 beetles. The population changes are not constant: the increases are 13, 16, and then only 2 beetles across successive food levels. The small increase from 20 to 30 g/day shows that adding food does not produce the same population increase at every level and that another limiting factor may become important.

g8s-cr-004.value: The data support an argument that the invasive shoreline plant may be affecting other wetland populations because after it spread, native shoreline plant cover fell from 72% to 31% and insect species recorded in equal sampling periods fell from 18 to 11, while water depth was similar. This association does not by itself prove causation. The argument would be strengthened by repeated measurements over time or comparison wetlands/sites without the invasive spread, while also measuring other relevant conditions such as water quality or temperature.

g8s-cr-005.value: The seasonal measurements show vegetation is associated with less short-term erosion: the bare 10 m bank lost 210 kg, the partly vegetated bank 122 kg, and the densely vegetated bank only 55 kg during comparable flow. Those are local, one-season measurements. The 25-year maps show the same kinds of erosion, transport, and deposition repeating across a river reach several kilometers long, with the channel shifting tens of meters. Repeated local sediment changes can therefore accumulate through time and across many bank sections into larger-scale changes in Earth's surface.

g8s-cr-006.value: Design A appears more effective. Its average use fell from 18,000 to 11,500 L/day, a reduction of 6,500 L/day, while Design B fell from 17,800 to 15,900 L/day, a reduction of only 1,900 L/day. Before broad adoption, the town should continue monitoring a factor that could change irrigation demand or performance over time, such as rainfall/weather and soil moisture, field use, or sensor/leak-repair maintenance, so the reduction remains attributable to the design under comparable conditions.
